description: Broad, explicit permissions for the installed app: open any URL/path in the OS, pick files, and run its own bundled server. Deliberately permissive per product decision — the app is local-first with a single user. A hardened build drops this capability and keeps only `default`. The served web app is also granted the shell commands that shape its own window and read its own diagnostics; the server lifecycle (`restart_server`, `stop_server`, `set_database_url`, `quit`) and the preference store (`get_pref`, `set_pref`, which holds the unredacted connection string) stay with the shell's own page. No file-system permissions: the app reads and writes its files server-side (Rust `std::fs`), never through the `fs` plugin, so the JavaScript face of that plugin stays unused here. The app's own data directories are covered by `fs:default` in the `default` capability, which is the narrow, local-only one.
